rationale: Timer bookkeeping: the rebuild sets the time since the compressor stopped back to 0 when the compressor STARTS. Setting line says that time starts again from 0 when the compressor turns off, and does not change while it runs. Never visible as heating or cooling in these situations, but a misread of a clear line.
Backup strips never come on while the compressor is heating, even 3 or more degrees below the setting. His backup rule has no such limit.

With no strips fitted, the rebuild gives no heat at all even with the outdoor temperature well above the cut-off. "No heat runs" belongs only to the cut-off rule (outdoor below the cut-off); above it the compressor heats.
Cooling comes on only above the setting plus the swing; "the same the other way" as the heat example means set to 70, swing 1, cooling at 71 or warmer.
